items.title: Candace Cameron Bure Addresses Distance From Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen
items.summary:
Candace Cameron Bure made a rare comment about the distance between the Full House cast and Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen .

During the Tuesday, November 24, episode of “The McBride Rewind” podcast, Cameron Bure, 50, was asked about attempts to bring the Olsen twins, 40, back for Netflix’s Fuller House revival in 2016.

“There were many calls,” she recalled. “No, [I didn’t call] because it wasn’t my show to pitch. I think that was between [creator] Jeff [Franklin] and John [Stamos] because it was really their show.”

Cameron Bure referred to Mary-Kate and Ashley’s decision not to make an appearance as “a bummer,” adding, “Because it would have been fun to have everybody back. But at the same time, it wasn’t surprising just because none of us really have stayed close with the girls.”

Where the ‘Full House’ Cast Stands With Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen 

She continued: “Not because anything went wrong or there was any bad blood. I just think they were kids. They were [filming from] 9 months old until they were 8 years old. They have very different memories than we do. Even me being 10 years older than them, I have significant, great, wonderful memories.”

Cameron Bure didn’t fault the former actresses for setting boundaries. 

“They were babies. They probably don’t even remember half the stuff [we do]. They didn’t have the attachment to the crew and the people like we did being older,” she explained. “And they had such a successful fashion business. They haven’t been actors for a long time. They just haven’t been in that part of entertainment.”

Warner Bros./ Courtesy: Everett…
items.t: Candace Cameron Bure Addresses Distance From Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen

items.title: Pittsburgh Steelers Announce Dramatic Aaron Rodgers News Amid Struggles
items.summary:
Aaron Rodgers will be spending Black Friday on the bench.  

The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that Rodgers, 42, will be “inactive” against the Denver Broncos on Friday, November 27, with backup quarterback Mason Rudolph taking his spot.  

The surprising move comes after two straight losses for the Steelers, both with Rodgers behind center. Pittsburgh lost in disappointing fashion to the Philadelphia Eagles, 19-16, on Sunday, November 22. Rodgers finished 30-for-44 passing with 227 yards and one touchdown.  

Pittsburgh is now 6-4 on the season tied for second place in the AFC North with the Cleveland Browns. Both teams are one game behind the first-place Cincinnati Bengals.  

Missing Coach Travis Turner's Wife Has Been 'Bullied to Death,' Neighbor Says 

After the loss to the Eagles, head coach Mike McCarthy scoffed at the idea of demoting Rodgers.  

“Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback,” McCarthy told reporters on Monday, November 23.  

However, ESPN reported on Wednesday, November 25, that the move to bench Rodgers was a coach’s decision.  

Sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that Rodgers was not in attendance at the Steelers’ 8 a.m. meeting Wednesday, and it is not clear whether he will attend Wednesday’s practice at noon.  

“The Steelers essentially believing that Mason Rudolph gives them the best chance to win,” Rapoport, 46, said on Wednesday . “So the big question is: What happened? Here’s my understanding of where the Steelers have been the last couple of days. They’ve had meetings — offensive meetings, staff meetings, meetings with players, meetings with…
items.t: Pittsburgh Steelers Announce Dramatic Aaron Rodgers News Amid Struggles

items.title: Jennifer Lopez Makes Rare Comment About 'Tough' Marc Anthony Divorce

Lopez candidly admits on stage that her separation from Anthony, 58, was “a really tough time,” as the couple had welcomed their twins, Max and Emme, only three years prior.

“It was one of those moments in life where you’re just about to give up on it all,” she reflects. “You’re just like, ‘I’ve given up on love. I’m giving up on life, the whole thing.’ But I had these two little baby twins, you know?”

items.title: 'DWTS' Champ Ezra Frech Says He 'Blacked Out' During Historic Freestyle
items.summary:
Ezra Frech made history as the first amputee and youngest man to win Dancing With the Stars alongside partner Daniella Karagach — but the victory still hasn’t set in.

“Last night was crazy. … I can’t believe this happened,” Frech, 21, said on Good Morning America just hours after the season 35 finale aired on Tuesday, November 24. “I can’t believe we got that opportunity to represent [the disabled community].”

For the season finale, the remaining five couples performed three separate dances, including the fan-favorite freestyle. Frech and Karagach, 33, earned a combined score of 90 out of 90 from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough , landing them in a three-way tie with Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov and Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas .

Before being announced as the winners, Frech and Karagach experienced a mishap in their live freestyle when the Paralympian struggled to get his prosthetic blade onto his leg.

'DWTS' Runner-Up Amber Glenn Breaks Silence After Emotional Finale 

“We started our freestyle without the prosthetic, that was a creative choice, and then things went a little off script,” Frech said on GMA . “I wasn’t able to suction my leg on and I knew it wasn’t on. Sometimes when that happens, it’ll re-suction, but it didn’t. It came off. She told me to put it on mid-dance, I kinda blacked out.”

items.title: WWE Star Thea Hail Shaves Head on Live TV Amid Alopecia Diagnosis at Age 23
items.summary:
WWE NXT star Thea Hail bravely shaved her head on live TV after being diagnosed with alopecia at age 23.

Back in August, Hail, real name Madison Knisley, shared via Instagram that she had alopecia areata, which, according to the Mayo Clinic , causes hair to fall out in patches. “Alopecia areata is a common autoimmune disorder affecting about 1 in every 1,000 people,” per the Mayo Clinic, with over 80% of people diagnosed with the condition showing signs of alopecia areata before the age of 40.

On the Tuesday, November 24, episode of WWE NXT on The CW, Hail got emotional as she addressed her progressive hair loss in front of the live audience at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida.

“You’re expected to walk through that curtain and look perfect,” Hail said through tears, acknowledging the beauty standards placed on women in professional wrestling.

10 Celebrities Facing Hair Loss, and What They Use To Fight It 

“I’m sure you can all imagine how afraid I was to share with the world that at 23 years old, I was diagnosed with alopecia,” she continued. “In less than four months, I lost about 40% of my hair. Since July, I’ve been asking myself the same questions you’re all probably wondering: will it grow back? How will I look? What does this mean? But most importantly, how will other people look at me if I have no hair?”

The former NXT Women’s North American Champion vowed to “take this moment of weakness and turn it into a strength” because “alopecia has been a bit of a blessing in disguise for me.”

items.title: Patrick Stewart Was 'Struggling With His Health' on 'Avengers: Doomsday' Set

The late Patrick Stewart managed to shoot one last movie before his death, but it was not without difficulty.

The legendary actor died in October from Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. He was 86.

Stewart’s final movie, Marvel Studios’ highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday , is set for release on December 18, and directors Anthony and Joe Russo , as well as Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige , recalled how he gave a speech on his final day on set.

“I think it was in the back of all of our heads [that] we may never see him on set again,” Anthony told Entertainment Weekly in an interview published on Tuesday, November 24.

Kyle MacLachlan and More Stars Mourn Patrick Stewart’s Death at 86 

“It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew,” Anthony continued.

Anthony added, “You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”
